name: Weekly sports recap videos from TheSportsDB (Zvid)

parameters.content:
## Weekly sports recap videos from TheSportsDB

Every Monday morning this workflow pulls your league's latest final scores
from TheSportsDB, has an LLM write the on-screen copy (headline, one punchy
line per match, sign-off), and renders a 1080x1920 scoreboard recap with
Zvid: hype title card over floodlit-stadium footage, one scoreboard scene
per match with the winner picked out in your accent colour, closing card
with your handle. No voiceover needed — the scores carry it, a music bed
drives it.

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **OpenRouter** — attach an **OpenRouter** credential to *Write recap*
   (any funded key; the default model costs pennies per run).
3. **Open `Config`** — set `brandName`, `handle` and `ctaText`. `leagueId`
   `4328` is the English Premier League; see the league note for others.
4. **Run it — the first run renders for real and spends about 24 credits.**
   When it finishes, click **▶ Watch video** to play the recap inside n8n.
5. Want a free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the
   exact credit quote plus an **editorLink**, nothing spent.
6. **Activate** — it posts a fresh recap every Monday at 8am.

### Cost per video

A five-match recap (~24 s) is about **24 credits**; fewer matches cost
less (a single-match recap is ~10 s ≈ 10 credits). *Validate project
(free)* quotes the exact figure before every render.

## Where the scores come from

*Fetch results* calls **TheSportsDB** (`eventspastleague.php`) with the
public test key `123` that ships in `Config`. Fine for trying the template,
but when this was authored that key returned only the **single most recent
result** — a personal key (cheap, thesportsdb.com) returns the last 15
finished fixtures and fills a full five-match recap. Put yours in
`sportsDbKey`.

| League | `leagueId` |
| --- | --- |
| English Premier League | 4328 |
| NBA | 4387 |
| NFL | 4391 |

More ids: open your league on thesportsdb.com — the id is in the URL.

**No key, API down, or off-season?** The run still renders: *Prepare
results* falls back to a bundled demo matchday (the real 2023-24 EPL final
day) and flags it with `usingDemoData: true` in the run summary.

## The scores are ground truth

The LLM (*Write recap*) writes **copy only** — the headline, one caption
per match, the sign-off. The numbers on screen come straight from
TheSportsDB; the model is told never to contradict them and is forbidden
from inventing scorers, minutes or incidents. A missing or broken caption
falls back to a plain scoreline ("Arsenal take it 2-1") instead of failing
the run.

Design details *Build project JSON* handles for you:

- Team names auto-shrink — "Wolverhampton Wanderers" wraps cleanly at
  38 px, short names get 56 px.
- Scores scale for double and triple digits (11-1 football, 112-98
  basketball), so NBA league ids work out of the box.
- The winner's side gets the accent colour plus an underline bar; draws
  stay neutral.
- The music bed is HEAD-checked first — an unreachable or oversized track
  drops the music rather than failing the render.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders for real.** Set it to
`true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates the
payload, quotes the exact credit cost and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the exact video and tweak anything by hand, with nothing
spent. Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

## Publishing the video (optional tail)

The workflow ends with the finished video URL in *Run summary* — a clean
handoff you can extend:

- **YouTube Shorts** — add an *HTTP Request* node (GET the `videoUrl`,
  response format `File`) followed by the native **YouTube** node
  (Video → Upload, binary `data`). Needs a YouTube OAuth2 credential.
- **Instagram / TikTok / everywhere** — pass `videoUrl` to a scheduler
  like Blotato, Buffer or Metricool via their HTTP API; they accept a
  public video URL directly, no download step needed.
- **Human in the loop** — a Slack or Email node that sends `videoUrl` to
  whoever posts manually.

They are left out of the required path on purpose so the template imports
and runs with a Zvid key and an OpenRouter key, nothing else.

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button — this week's recap, no URL to copy.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`, `usingDemoData`) if you want to pipe the result onward.
